page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance from the E2 family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the instance is optimized for memory capacity rather than raw compute speed. The Passmark memory score is in the average tier, and the LLM text generation speed for a small 135M model also registers in the average range at 102.59 tokens per second. However, CPU-bound benchmarks are consistently positioned in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU metrics fall in the bottom 25%, while Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are in the bottom 10%. Similarly, static web serving throughput is limited to 2.66 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations reach 2.61 million operations per second, both placing in the lower performance brackets.

The e2-highmem-4 offers a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for workloads that require a larger memory footprint but have modest CPU demands. Because memory is prioritized over compute power, users avoid paying for high-performance CPU architectures when their applications are primarily memory-bound. The primary tradeoff is the weak single-threaded and multi-threaded processing capability, as evidenced by poor compression and decompression speeds. This hardware profile is best suited for memory-intensive tasks with low CPU utilization, such as caching layers, small database operations, and lightweight background workers.
